result:
Moses was a man chosen by God.  It took him 40 days and 40 nights to come down from Mount Sinai with the tablets in his hand.  God had spoken to him and he had been in the mountain contemplating God's holiness.  The Lord instructed Moses to go down and summon the people.  But when Moses met Aaron and his two sons, he complained about his grievances.  The Lord saw how he was being afraid and unable to face the Egyptians, and the Lord rebuked him for failing to follow the commands of God.

The Rebuke had been effective, and Moses did as God had commanded.  He went to the crowd and proclaimed, "Let my people go", and even when the Egyptian Pharaoh rebuffed him, he did nothing but grow in faith. Not fear, but faith. When we are faced with challenges in our lives, we often reach for closure or for certainties, and we find all too often that life is not like our scriptures. We find that there is neither certainty nor closure. Instead, we find that where we hold onto god's power and presence in our lives, the Lord provides in ways that we would never have imagined.

God's love is always there.  It finds us and guides even in times when it seems impossible and in ways that we cannot immediately comprehend nor always understand.  God is a God of sorrys.  We fail and we struggle, and sometimes those failures bring us to a place where we find new strength, patience, and hope.  Moses' faithfulness was tested by every obstacle and every task that came his way.  It was nothing but his unwavering faith that drew him to God and kept him grounded.

Learn from Moses and remember his story to find courage during your toughest times.  God gives us a rod, a way to command people through faith.  This strength in faith helps us to go forward, to trust, and to come out stronger on the other side, just as God intended for Moses.  God's strength lies within, a source of power strong enough to overcome any onslaught or failure.  We find that power in our own life to trust in God.

Reach out to God.  Ask for help, let the Lord inspire you.  Treat it as part of your renewal.  Remind yourself that you are not alone in your struggles.  Let God be the rock that you turn to, through every ebb and flow.  When you rely on Him, you will find yourself soaring high, with God's steadfast love to guide you every step of the way. Psalm 115:1-2 says, "LORD, who may abide the day of Your wrath? And who shall stand? But blessed be the LORD God of Israel, who travels in the stead of his people; his arm goes out to save his anointed, and his righteousness shall deliver him."
